label: Figure 12.2: The demand curve facing a monopolist
alt: A monopolist's downward-sloping D=AR curve with a steeper MR curve below it and an upward-sloping MC curve, selling quantity q at price P where MC=MR.
caption: The monopolist faces the whole market’s downward-sloping demand curve, D = AR, with a steeper MR curve below it. It maximizes profit by producing where MC = MR, at output q, and charges the price P read up from q to the demand curve. Because the firm controls the entire industry’s output, it can restrict quantity below what a price taker would supply in order to raise price — this is the essence of monopoly power.
